title.zh: 卷83下 外戚下:高肇 于勁 胡國珍 李延實
title.en: Volume 83b: Families of Imperial Consorts 2 - Gao Zhao, Yu Jin, Hu Guozhen, Li Yanshi
title.raw: 卷83下 外戚下:高肇 于勁 胡國珍 李延實 Volume 83b: Families of Imperial Consorts 2 - Gao Zhao, Yu Jin, Hu Guozhen, Li Yanshi

sentences.zh: 高肇 于勁 胡國珍 李延寔

translations.literal: Gao Zhao; Yu Jin; Hu Guozhen; Li Yanshi
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao; Yu Jin; Hu Guozhen; Li Yanshi

sentences.zh: 高肇，字首文，文昭皇太后之兄也。

translations.literal: Gao Zhao, styled Shouwen, was the elder brother of Empress Dowager Wen Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao, courtesy name Shouwen, was the elder brother of Empress Dowager Wen Zhao.

sentences.zh: 自云本勃海蓨人，五世祖顧，晉永嘉中避亂入高麗。

translations.literal: He himself said that his family were originally from Tiao in Bohai; his fifth-generation ancestor Gu, in the Yongjia era of Jin, fled turmoil and entered Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed descent from Tiao in Bohai. His fifth-generation ancestor Gu had fled the disorders of the Jin Yongjia era and taken refuge in Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 父颺，字法脩。

translations.literal: His father was Yang, styled Faxing.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Yang, courtesy name Faxing.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，與弟乘信及其鄉人韓內、冀富等入國，拜厲威將軍、河間子，乘信明威將軍，俱待以客禮，賜奴婢牛馬綵帛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's reign, together with his younger brother Chengxin and his fellow townsmen Han Nei, Ji Fu, and others, he entered the state; he was appointed General of Illustrious Might and Marquis of Hejian, Chengxin was appointed General of Bright Prestige, and both were received with guest ritual and granted male and female slaves, cattle, horses, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Gaozu, he entered the kingdom with his younger brother Chengxin and fellow townsmen Han Nei, Ji Fu, and others. He was made General of Illustrious Might and Marquis of Hejian; Chengxin was made General of Bright Prestige. Both were received as honored guests and given slaves, horses, cattle, and silks.

sentences.zh: 遂納颺女，是為文昭皇后，生世宗。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took Yang's daughter in marriage; she became Empress Wen Zhao and bore Emperor Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: He then married Yang's daughter, who became Empress Wen Zhao and bore Emperor Shizong.

sentences.zh: 颺卒。

translations.literal: Yang died.
translations.idiomatic: Yang died.

sentences.zh: 景明初，世宗追思舅氏，徵肇兄弟等。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming, Emperor Shizong, thinking of his mother's kin, summoned Zhao and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingming era, Emperor Shizong, mindful of his mother's family, summoned Zhao and his brothers to court.

sentences.zh: 錄尚書事、北海王詳等奏：「颺宜贈左光祿大夫，賜爵勃海公，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing and Prince of Beihai, Xiang, and others memorialized: "Yang should be posthumously granted Left Grand Master of the Palace, enfeoffed as Duke of Bohai, and given the posthumous title Jing."
translations.idiomatic: The Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Beihai Xiang, and others submitted a memorial: "Yang should be posthumously granted the title Left Grand Master of the Palace, enfeoffed as Duke of Bohai, and given the posthumous epithet Jing."

sentences.zh: 其妻蓋氏宜追封清河郡君。

translations.literal: His wife, the Lady Gai, should be posthumously ennobled as Lady of Qinghe Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Gai, should be posthumously ennobled as Lady of Qinghe Commandery.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 又詔颺嫡孫猛襲勃海公爵，封肇平原郡公，肇弟顯澄城郡公。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered that Yang's eldest grandson by the principal wife, Meng, should inherit the ducal title of Bohai; Zhao was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan Commandery, and Zhao's younger brother Xian as Duke of Chengcheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict appointed Yang's legitimate grandson Meng to succeed to the dukedom of Bohai, enfeoffed Zhao as Duke of Pingyuan Commandery, and Zhao's younger brother Xian as Duke of Chengcheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 三人同日受封。

translations.literal: All three received enfeoffment on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: All three were enfeoffed on the same day.

sentences.zh: 始世宗未與舅氏相接，將拜爵，乃賜衣幘引見肇、顯于華林都亭。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Shizong had not yet met his mother's kin; when he was about to confer ranks, he granted them caps and garments and had Zhao and Xian led in to be received at the Du Pavilion in Hualin.
translations.idiomatic: Until then Emperor Shizong had never met his maternal uncles. Before conferring their titles, he gave them caps and robes and received Zhao and Xian at the Du Pavilion in Hualin Park.

sentences.zh: 皆甚惶懼，舉動失儀。

translations.literal: Both were greatly fearful and alarmed, and their movements were unseemly.
translations.idiomatic: Both were deeply frightened, and their deportment was altogether unseemly.

sentences.zh: 數日之間，富貴赫弈。

translations.literal: Within a few days, wealth and honor blazed forth.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days they had risen to dazzling wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 是年，咸陽王禧誅，財物珍寶奴婢田宅多入高氏。

translations.literal: That year, Prince of Xianyang, Xi, was executed, and goods, treasures, slaves, fields, and houses largely passed into the Gao clan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Prince of Xianyang Xi was put to death, and much of his property, treasure, slaves, fields, and houses passed to the Gao family.

sentences.zh: 未幾，肇為尚書左僕射、領吏部、冀州大中正，尚世宗姑高平公主，遷尚書令。

translations.literal: Before long, Zhao became Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, concurrently head of the Ministry of Personnel and Grand Rectifier of Jizhou; he married Emperor Shizong's paternal aunt, the Princess of Gaoping, and was promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhao was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, head of the Ministry of Personnel, and Grand Rectifier of Jizhou. He married Emperor Shizong's paternal aunt, the Princess of Gaoping, and was promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 肇出自夷土，時望輕之。

translations.literal: Zhao came from barbarian lands, and men of the time held him in light esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhao came from foreign soil, contemporaries looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 及在位居要，留心百揆，孜孜無倦，世咸謂之為能。

translations.literal: When he reached an important post, he attended to the hundred affairs of state, diligent and untiring, and the age all called him capable.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held high office, he attended closely to affairs of state, working tirelessly, and the world at large regarded him as capable.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，六輔專政，後以咸陽王禧無事構逆，由是遂委信肇。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, the six chief ministers monopolized government; later, because Prince of Xianyang, Xi, without cause plotted rebellion, he thereupon entrusted Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shizong's reign the six chief ministers monopolized power. Later, when Prince of Xianyang Xi plotted rebellion without cause, the emperor placed his trust in Zhao instead.

sentences.zh: 肇既無親族，頗結朋黨，附之者旬月超昇，背之者陷以大罪。

translations.literal: Zhao had no kin of his own and rather formed factions; those who attached to him were promoted within a month, while those who turned against him were trapped in great crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao had no family at court and instead built a faction. Supporters were promoted within a month; opponents were ruined on grave charges.

sentences.zh: 以北海王詳位居其上，構殺之。

translations.literal: Because Prince of Beihai, Xiang, stood above him in rank, he framed him and had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Beihai Xiang outranked him, so Zhao framed him and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 又說世宗防衞諸王，殆同囚禁。

translations.literal: He also urged Emperor Shizong to guard the princes, so that they were nearly like prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: He also persuaded Emperor Shizong to place the princes under heavy guard, so that they were kept almost like prisoners.

sentences.zh: 時順皇后暴崩，世議言肇為之。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Shun died suddenly; public opinion said Zhao was responsible.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Shun died suddenly, public rumor blamed Zhao.

sentences.zh: 皇子昌薨，僉謂王顯失於醫療，承肇意旨。

translations.literal: The imperial son Chang died; all said Wang Xian had failed in medical treatment, carrying out Zhao's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial son Chang died, many believed the physician Wang Xian had bungled his care at Zhao's bidding.

sentences.zh: 及京兆王愉出為冀州刺史，畏肇恣擅，遂至不軌。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jingzhao, Yu, went out as Governor of Jizhou, he feared Zhao's arbitrary power and thus came to misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Jingzhao Yu went out to Jizhou as governor, he feared Zhao's arbitrary rule and eventually rebelled.

sentences.zh: 肇又譖殺彭城王勰。

translations.literal: Zhao again slandered and killed Prince of Pengcheng, Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao also slandered Prince of Pengcheng Xie and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 由是朝野側目，咸畏惡之。

translations.literal: Because of this, court and countryside looked askance, and all feared and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on court and countryside alike watched him with hostility, and all feared and hated him.

sentences.zh: 因此專權，與奪任己。

translations.literal: Because of this he monopolized power, granting and taking away as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore monopolized power, granting and taking away offices as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 又嘗與清河王懌於雲龍門外廡下，忽忿諍，大至紛紜。

translations.literal: He also once, with Prince of Qinghe, Yi, under the corridor outside the Yunlong Gate, suddenly quarreled in anger, to the point of great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He once quarreled heatedly with Prince of Qinghe Yi in the corridor outside the Yunlong Gate, and the dispute nearly came to blows.

sentences.zh: 太尉、高陽王雍和止之。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal and Prince of Gaoyang, Yong, harmonized and stopped them.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Prince of Gaoyang Yong intervened and stopped them.

sentences.zh: 高后既立，愈見寵信。

translations.literal: After Empress Gao was established, he was ever more favored and trusted.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Gao was enthroned, he grew still more favored and trusted.

sentences.zh: 肇既當衡軸，每事任己，本無學識，動違禮度，好改先朝舊制，出情妄作，減削封秩，抑黜勳人。

translations.literal: Zhao, now holding the pivot of power, on every matter followed his own will; he originally had no learning, and his actions often violated ritual norms; he liked to alter the old institutions of former courts, acting capriciously from personal feeling, reducing enfeoffments and ranks and demoting men of merit.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhao held the reins of government, he did as he pleased in every matter. He had little learning and often violated ritual propriety. He liked to overturn former institutions, acting on whim, cutting ranks and enfeoffments and pushing aside men of merit.

sentences.zh: 由是怨聲盈路矣。

translations.literal: Because of this, sounds of resentment filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Complaints against him filled the land.

sentences.zh: 延昌初，遷司徒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yan Chang, he was transferred to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yan Chang era he was made Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 雖貴登台鼎，猶以去要怏怏形乎辭色。

translations.literal: Although ennobled to ascend the tripod of state, he still showed displeasure at leaving key posts in his words and countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had risen to one of the highest offices, he still showed his resentment at losing real power in his words and expression.

sentences.zh: 眾咸嗤笑之。

translations.literal: The multitude all mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 父兄封贈雖久，竟不改瘞。

translations.literal: Although his father and elder brothers had long received posthumous enfeoffment, he still did not change their burial.
translations.idiomatic: Although his father and elder brothers had long received posthumous honors, he still did not have their remains reburied.

sentences.zh: 三年，乃詔令遷葬。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict finally ordered their reburial.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year an edict finally ordered their remains moved.

sentences.zh: 肇不自臨赴，唯遣其兄子猛改服詣代，遷葬於鄉。

translations.literal: Zhao did not go in person; he only sent his elder brother's son Meng, changing into mourning garments and going to Dai, to transfer the burial to their native place.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao did not go himself. He sent only his nephew Meng, dressed in mourning, to Dai to move the remains home for reburial.

sentences.zh: 時人以肇無識，哂而不責也。

translations.literal: Men of the time, because Zhao lacked understanding, only sneered and did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries, deeming Zhao ignorant, only sneered and did not hold it against him.

sentences.zh: 其年，大舉征蜀，以肇為大將軍，都督諸軍為之節度。

translations.literal: That year, a great campaign was launched against Shu; Zhao was made Grand General and put in overall command of the armies as their director.
translations.idiomatic: That year a major campaign was launched against Shu. Zhao was made Grand General and given overall command of the armies.

sentences.zh: 與都督甄琛等二十餘人俱面辭世宗於東堂，親奉規略。

translations.literal: Together with the commander Zhen Chen and more than twenty others, he took leave of Emperor Shizong face to face in the Eastern Hall and personally received strategic instructions.
translations.idiomatic: He and more than twenty commanders, including Zhen Chen, took leave of Emperor Shizong in the Eastern Hall and received the emperor's strategy in person.

sentences.zh: 是日，肇所乘駿馬停於神虎門外，無故驚倒，轉臥渠中，鞍具瓦解，眾咸怪異。

translations.literal: That day, the fine horse Zhao rode halted outside the Shenhu Gate, startled and fallen for no reason, rolling into a ditch; saddle and trappings came apart, and the crowd all regarded it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: That day Zhao's mount, waiting outside the Shenhu Gate, suddenly bolted and fell into a ditch, shattering its saddle and trappings. Everyone regarded it as an ill omen.

sentences.zh: 肇出，惡焉。

translations.literal: When Zhao went out, he regarded it as ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao took it as a bad sign when he set out.

sentences.zh: 四年，世宗崩，赦罷征軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Emperor Shizong died; an amnesty was issued and the expeditionary army was disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Emperor Shizong died. An amnesty was proclaimed and the expeditionary army was recalled.

sentences.zh: 肅宗與肇及征南將軍元遙等書，稱諱言，以告凶問。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong wrote to Zhao and the General Who Conquers the South, Yuan Yao, and others, using the tabooed words to announce the grievous news.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong wrote to Zhao, General Who Conquers the South Yuan Yao, and the others, using the prescribed taboo language to announce the emperor's death.

sentences.zh: 肇承變哀愕，非唯仰慕，亦私憂身禍，朝夕悲泣，至于羸悴。

translations.literal: Zhao, receiving the change, was mournful and stunned; it was not only admiration, but also private fear of personal disaster; morning and evening he wept in grief until he was emaciated and haggard.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao received the news he was stunned with grief. It was not only mourning for the emperor; he also feared for his own life, weeping day and night until he was wasted and haggard.

sentences.zh: 將至，宿瀍澗驛亭，家人夜迎省之，皆不相視。

translations.literal: As he was about to arrive, he lodged at the post station at Chanjian; his family came by night to receive and visit him, and none could look at one another.
translations.idiomatic: As he neared the capital he lodged at the Chanjian post station. His family came out at night to see him, but none could bear to meet one another's eyes.

sentences.zh: 直至闕下，衰服號哭，昇太極殿，奉喪盡哀。

translations.literal: He went straight to below the palace gate, in mourning garments wailing and crying, ascended the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and attended the coffin with full grief.
translations.idiomatic: He went straight to the palace gate in mourning dress, wailing aloud. He ascended the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and mourned the coffin with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 太尉高陽王先居西柏堂，專決庶事，與領軍于忠密欲除之。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal, Prince of Gaoyang, had first occupied the Western Cypress Hall and alone decided common affairs; together with the Commander of the Guards, Yu Zhong, he secretly wished to eliminate Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Prince of Gaoyang Yong had already taken up residence in the Western Cypress Hall and controlled routine government. He and Commander of the Guards Yu Zhong secretly plotted to kill Zhao.

sentences.zh: 潛備壯士直寢邢豹、伊瓫生等十餘人於舍人省下。

translations.literal: They secretly stationed more than ten stalwart men of the direct guard, Xing Bao, Yi Qiusheng, and others, under the Office of Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: They secretly posted more than ten strongmen of the inner guard, including Xing Bao and Yi Qiusheng, in the Office of Attendants.

sentences.zh: 肇哭梓宮訖，於百官前引入西廊，清河王懌、任城王澄及諸王等皆竊言目之。

translations.literal: When Zhao had finished mourning before the imperial coffin, he was led before the hundred officials into the western corridor; Prince of Qinghe, Yi, Prince of Rencheng, Cheng, and the other princes all whispered and watched him.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhao had finished mourning before the coffin, he was led before the assembled officials into the western corridor. Prince of Qinghe Yi, Prince of Rencheng Cheng, and the other princes whispered among themselves as they watched.

sentences.zh: 肇入省，壯士搤而拉殺之。

translations.literal: When Zhao entered the inner office, the stalwarts seized him and strangled him to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao entered the inner office, the strongmen seized him and strangled him to death.

sentences.zh: 下詔暴其罪惡，又云刑書未及，便至自盡，自餘親黨，悉無追問，削除職爵，葬以士禮。

translations.literal: An edict was issued exposing his crimes; it also said that before the penal documents had arrived, he had come to self-destruction; the rest of his kin and associates were not pursued; his offices and ranks were struck off, and he was buried with commoner's rites.
translations.idiomatic: An edict exposed his crimes and declared that he had taken his own life before formal sentence could be passed. His other kin and associates were not prosecuted. His offices and titles were revoked, and he was buried with commoner's rites.

sentences.zh: 及昏，乃於厠門出其尸歸家。

translations.literal: At dusk, they then took his corpse out through the privy gate and returned it to his home.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk his body was taken out through the privy gate and sent home.

sentences.zh: 初，肇西征，行至函谷，車軸中折。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhao marched west on campaign, as he reached Hangu Pass the axle of his carriage broke in the middle.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, on his western campaign, Zhao's carriage axle had snapped in two at Hangu Pass.

sentences.zh: 從者皆以為不獲吉還也。

translations.literal: His followers all thought he would not obtain a fortunate return.
translations.idiomatic: His followers had all taken it as a sign that he would not return safely.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，令特贈營州刺史。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, she ordered special posthumous grant as Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling assumed regency, she ordered him specially posthumously granted the post of Governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年，出帝贈使持節、侍中、中外諸軍事、太師、大丞相、太尉公、錄尚書事、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, Emperor Chu granted him Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies Within and Without, Grand Preceptor, Grand Chancellor, Duke of Grand Marshal, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi Emperor Chu posthumously granted him Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies Within and Without, Grand Preceptor, Grand Chancellor, Duke of Grand Marshal, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 肇子植。

translations.literal: Zhao's son Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's son Zhi.

sentences.zh: 自中書侍郎為濟州刺史，率州軍討破元愉，別將有功。

translations.literal: From Palace Secretariat Attendant he became Governor of Jizhou, led the provincial army to defeat and subdue Yuan Yu, and as a separate commander had merit.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as Palace Secretariat Attendant he became Governor of Jizhou. He led the provincial army to defeat Yuan Yu and distinguished himself as a separate commander.

sentences.zh: 當蒙封賞，不受，云：「家荷重恩，為國致效是其常節，何足以應進陟之報。

translations.literal: He ought to have received enfeoffment and reward, but he did not accept, saying: "Our house has received heavy grace; to render service to the state is our constant duty—how could that suffice as repayment for advancement and promotion?"
translations.idiomatic: He was due for enfeoffment and reward but refused, saying, "Our family has received great favor from the throne. Serving the state is our plain duty—how could that merit promotion in return?"

sentences.zh: 」懇惻發於至誠。

translations.literal: " His earnest sincerity sprang from utmost truth.
translations.idiomatic: " His earnestness came from genuine conviction.

sentences.zh: 歷青、相、朔、恒四州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: He successively held the governorships of Qing, Xiang, Shuo, and Heng provinces, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as governor of Qing, Xiang, Shuo, and Heng provinces, then died.

sentences.zh: 植頻莅五州，皆清能著稱，當時號為良刺史。

translations.literal: Zhi repeatedly governed five provinces; in all he was renowned for integrity and ability, and men of the time called him a good governor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi governed five provinces in all, earning a reputation for integrity and competence, and his contemporaries hailed him as an excellent governor.

sentences.zh: 贈安北將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 肇長兄琨，早卒。

translations.literal: Zhao's elder brother Kun died early.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's elder brother Kun died young.

sentences.zh: 襲颺封勃海郡公，贈都督五州諸軍事、鎮東大將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He inherited Yang's enfeoffment as Duke of Bohai Commandery and was posthumously granted Commander-in-Chief of the Armies of Five Provinces, General Who Guards the East, and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited Yang's title as Duke of Bohai Commandery and was posthumously granted Commander-in-Chief of the Armies of Five Provinces, General Who Guards the East, and Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 詔其子猛嗣。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his son Meng to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed his son Meng as successor.

sentences.zh: 猛，字豹兒。

translations.literal: Meng, styled Bao'er.
translations.idiomatic: Meng, courtesy name Bao'er.

sentences.zh: 尚長樂公主，即世宗同母妹也。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Changle, who was Emperor Shizong's younger sister by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Changle, Emperor Shizong's younger uterine sister.

sentences.zh: 拜駙馬都尉，歷位中書令。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commandant of Escort Cavalry and rose to Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Commandant of Escort Cavalry and later served as Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出為雍州刺史，有能名。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Yongzhou and had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to Yongzhou as governor and earned a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 入為殿中尚書。

translations.literal: He entered court as Director of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Director of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Minister of Works and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted Minister of Works and Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 出帝時，復贈太師、大丞相、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Chu, he was again granted Grand Preceptor, Grand Chancellor, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Chu he was again posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, Grand Chancellor, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 公主無子。

translations.literal: The princess had no son.
translations.idiomatic: The princess had no children.

sentences.zh: 猛先在外有男，不敢令主知，臨終方言之，年幾三十矣。

translations.literal: Meng had earlier had a son while away and did not dare let his mistress know; only at his deathbed did he speak of it—the boy was nearly thirty.
translations.idiomatic: Meng had earlier fathered a son while away from home but dared not tell the princess. Only on his deathbed did he reveal the boy, who was nearly thirty.

sentences.zh: 乃召為喪主，尋卒，無後。

translations.literal: He was then summoned to serve as chief mourner; soon he died, leaving no heir.
translations.idiomatic: The son was summoned to lead the mourning, but he soon died too, and the line ended.

sentences.zh: 琨弟偃，字仲游。

translations.literal: Kun's younger brother Yan, styled Zhongyou.
translations.idiomatic: Kun's younger brother Yan, courtesy name Zhongyou.

sentences.zh: 太和十年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the tenth year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 正始中，贈安東將軍、都督、青州刺史，諡曰莊侯。

translations.literal: In Zhengshi he was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East, Commander-in-Chief, and Governor of Qingzhou, with the posthumous title Marquis Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengshi era he was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East, Commander-in-Chief, and Governor of Qingzhou, with the posthumous epithet Marquis Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 景明四年，世宗納其女為貴嬪。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingming, Emperor Shizong took his daughter as Honored Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jingming Emperor Shizong took his daughter as Honored Consort.

sentences.zh: 及于順皇后崩，永平元年立為皇后。

translations.literal: When Empress Shun of the Yu clan died, in the first year of Yongping she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Shun of the Yu clan died, she was enthroned as empress in the first year of Yongping.

sentences.zh: 二年，八座奏封后母王氏為武邑郡君。

translations.literal: In the second year, the eight chief ministers memorialized to enfeoff the empress's mother, the Lady Wang, as Lady of Wuyi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the eight chief ministers memorialized to enfeoff the empress's mother, Lady Wang, as Lady of Wuyi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 偃弟壽，早卒。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Shou died early.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Shou died young.

sentences.zh: 壽弟即肇也。

translations.literal: Shou's younger brother was none other than Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Shou's younger brother was Zhao himself.

sentences.zh: 肇弟顯，侍中、高麗國大中正，早卒。

translations.literal: Zhao's younger brother Xian, Palace Attendant and Grand Rectifier of the State of Goguryeo, died early.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's younger brother Xian, who had served as Palace Attendant and Grand Rectifier of Goguryeo, also died young.

sentences.zh: 于勁，字鍾葵，太尉拔之子。

translations.literal: Yu Jin, styled Zhongkui, was the son of the Grand Marshal Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin, courtesy name Zhongkui, was the son of Grand Marshal Ba.

sentences.zh: 頗有武略。

translations.literal: He had considerable military stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 以功臣子，又以功績，位沃野鎮將，賜爵富昌子，拜征虜將軍。

translations.literal: As the son of a meritorious minister, and again for his own achievements, he held the post of garrison commander of Woye, was granted the title Marquis of Fuchang, and was appointed General Who Punishes the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: As the son of a meritorious minister and for his own achievements, he became garrison commander of Woye, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fuchang, and was appointed General Who Punishes the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 世宗納其女為后，封太原郡公。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong took his daughter as empress, and he was enfeoffed as Duke of Taiyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong took his daughter as empress, and Jin was enfeoffed as Duke of Taiyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 妻劉氏，為章武郡君。

translations.literal: His wife, the Lady Liu, was made Lady of Zhangwu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Liu, was ennobled as Lady of Zhangwu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 後拜征北將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Campaigns North and Governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed General Who Campaigns North and Governor of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空，諡曰恭莊公。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Minister of Works, with the posthumous title Duke Gongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted Minister of Works, with the posthumous epithet Duke Gongzhuang.

sentences.zh: 自栗磾至勁，累世貴盛，一皇后，四贈公，三領軍，二尚書令，三開國公。

translations.literal: From Li Dili to Jin, generation after generation was noble and flourishing: one empress, four posthumously granted dukes, three commanders of the guards, two directors of the masters of writing, and three founding marquises.
translations.idiomatic: From Li Dili down to Jin, the family had been eminent for generations: one empress, four men posthumously made dukes, three commanders of the guards, two directors of the masters of writing, and three founding marquises.

sentences.zh: [2]勁雖以后父，但以順后早崩，竟不居公輔。

translations.literal: [2] Although Jin was father of the empress, because Empress Shun died early, he never in the end held the rank of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: [2] Though Jin was the empress's father, Empress Shun died young, and he never rose to chief minister.

sentences.zh: 子暉，字宣明，后母弟也。

translations.literal: His son Hui, styled Xuanming, was the empress's younger uterine brother.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui, courtesy name Xuanming, was the empress's younger uterine brother.

sentences.zh: 少有氣幹。

translations.literal: In youth he had spirit and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed force of character and ability.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，位汾州刺史。

translations.literal: He inherited the title and held the post of Governor of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the family title and served as Governor of Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 暉善事人，為尒朱榮所親，以女妻其子長孺。

translations.literal: Hui was skilled at winning people; Erzhu Rong favored him and gave him his daughter in marriage to his son Changru.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was skilled at winning people over. Erzhu Rong favored him and gave him his daughter as wife for his son Changru.

sentences.zh: 歷侍中、河南尹，後兼尚書僕射、東南道行臺。

translations.literal: He successively held Palace Attendant and Intendant of Henan; later he concurrently served as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Commissioner of the Southeastern Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Palace Attendant and Intendant of Henan, and later as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Commissioner of the Southeastern Circuit.

sentences.zh: 與齊獻武王討平羊侃於兗州。

translations.literal: Together with the Prince of Qi Who Offered the Kingdom, he suppressed and pacified Yang Kan in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Prince of Qi Who Offered the Kingdom, he put down Yang Kan's rebellion in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，害之。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, he killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, he had Hui killed.

sentences.zh: 勁弟天恩，位內行長、遼西太守。

translations.literal: Jin's younger brother Tian'en held the posts of Director of the Inner Service and Governor of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's younger brother Tian'en served as Director of the Inner Service and Governor of Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈平東將軍、燕州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 天恩子仁生，位太中大夫。

translations.literal: Tian'en's son Rensheng held the post of Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Tian'en's son Rensheng served as Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 仁生子安定，平原郡太守、高平郡都將。

translations.literal: Rensheng's son was Anding, Governor of Pingyuan Commandery and Commander-in-Chief of Gaoping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Rensheng's son Anding served as Governor of Pingyuan Commandery and Commander-in-Chief of Gaoping Commandery.

translations.literal: [3] He died.
translations.idiomatic: [3] He died.

sentences.zh: 胡國珍，字世玉，安定臨涇人也。

translations.literal: Hu Guozhen, styled Shiyu, was a native of Linjing in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guozhen, courtesy name Shiyu, was a native of Linjing in Anding.

sentences.zh: 祖略，姚興渤海公姚逵平北府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lue was a staff adviser in the Northern Pacification Office of Yao Kui, Duke of Bohai under Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lue had served as staff adviser in the Northern Pacification Office of Yao Kui, Duke of Bohai, under Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 父淵，赫連屈丐給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Yuan was Attendant at the Yellow Gate under Helian Qugai.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan had served as Attendant at the Yellow Gate under Helian Qugai.

sentences.zh: 世祖克統萬，淵以降款之功賜爵武始侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu conquered Tongwan, Yuan was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wushi for the merit of surrendering in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu conquered Tongwan, Yuan was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wushi for surrendering in good faith.

sentences.zh: 後拜河州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Governor of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 國珍少好學，雅尚清儉。

translations.literal: Guozhen in youth loved learning and elegantly esteemed purity and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen loved learning from youth and prized simplicity and frugality.

sentences.zh: 太和十五年襲爵，例降為伯。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Taihe he inherited the title, and by precedent it was reduced to Earl.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Taihe he inherited the family title, which by precedent was reduced to earl.

sentences.zh: 女以選入掖庭，生肅宗，即靈太后也。

translations.literal: His daughter was selected to enter the Rear Palace, bore Emperor Suzong, and was none other than Empress Dowager Ling.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter was selected for the imperial harem, bore Emperor Suzong, and became Empress Dowager Ling.

sentences.zh: 肅宗踐祚，以國珍為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong ascended the throne, he appointed Guozhen Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong came to the throne, he appointed Guozhen Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，加侍中，封安定郡公，給甲第，賜帛布綿縠奴婢車馬牛甚厚。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, he was further made Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Duke of Anding Commandery; a fine mansion was granted, and silks, cloth, cotton, damasks, slaves, carriages, horses, and cattle were bestowed in great abundance.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling assumed regency, he was made Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Duke of Anding Commandery. She granted him a fine mansion and lavish gifts of silks, cloth, slaves, carriages, horses, and cattle.

sentences.zh: 追崇國珍妻皇甫氏為京兆郡君，置守冢十戶。

translations.literal: Guozhen's wife, the Lady Huangfu, was posthumously honored as Lady of Jingzhao Commandery, and ten households were established to guard the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen's wife, Lady Huangfu, was posthumously honored as Lady of Jingzhao Commandery, and ten households were assigned to tend the tomb.

sentences.zh: 尚書令、任城王澄奏，安定公屬尊望重，親賢羣矚，宜出入禁中，參諮大務。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing and Prince of Rencheng, Cheng, memorialized: "The Duke of Anding, by kinship honored and by reputation weighty, is gazed upon by the multitude of kin and worthies; he should enter and leave within the forbidden precincts and take part in consulting on great affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Prince of Rencheng Cheng memorialized: "The Duke of Anding is eminent in rank and reputation, and the court looks to him as kin and elder. He should have access to the inner palace and advise on great affairs of state."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 乃令入決萬幾。

translations.literal: He was then ordered to enter and decide the myriad affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was then authorized to take part in deciding state affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋進位中書監、儀同三司，侍中如故，賞賜累萬。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat and Honored with the Three Insignia, remaining Palace Attendant as before; rewards and gifts piled into the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat and Honored with the Three Insignia while retaining his post as Palace Attendant. Rewards poured in by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 又賜絹歲八百匹，妻梁四百匹，男女姊妹兄弟各有差，皆極豐贍。

translations.literal: He was further granted eight hundred bolts of silk yearly, his wife the Lady Liang four hundred bolts, and sons, daughters, sisters, and brothers each in differing amounts—all extremely ample.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted eight hundred bolts of silk a year, his wife Lady Liang four hundred, and sons, daughters, sisters, and brothers each received lavish shares.

sentences.zh: 國珍與太師、高陽王雍，太傅、清河王懌，太保、廣平王懷，入居門下，同釐庶政。

translations.literal: Guozhen, together with Grand Preceptor and Prince of Gaoyang, Yong, Grand Tutor and Prince of Qinghe, Yi, and Grand Guardian and Prince of Guangping, Huai, entered and dwelt in the Gate Below, jointly ordering common government.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen joined Grand Preceptor Prince of Gaoyang Yong, Grand Tutor Prince of Qinghe Yi, and Grand Guardian Prince of Guangping Huai in the Gate Below to oversee routine government together.

sentences.zh: 詔依漢車千秋、晉安平王故事，給步挽一乘，自掖門至于宣光殿得以出入，并備几杖。

translations.literal: An edict followed the precedents of Han's Che Qianqiu and Jin's Prince of Ping'an, granting one hand-drawn carriage; from the Yebi Gate to the Hall of Proclaiming Light he was permitted to enter and leave, and a couch and staff were also provided.
translations.idiomatic: By edict, following the precedents of Han's Che Qianqiu and Jin's Prince of Ping'an, he was given a hand-drawn carriage and allowed to pass from the Yebi Gate to the Hall of Proclaiming Light. A couch and staff were also provided.

sentences.zh: 後與侍中崔光俱授帝經，侍直禁中。

translations.literal: Later, together with Palace Attendant Cui Guang, he instructed the emperor in the classics and attended on duty within the forbidden precincts.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Palace Attendant Cui Guang together instructed the emperor in the classics and kept watch within the palace.

sentences.zh: 國珍尋上表，陳刑政之宜。

translations.literal: Before long Guozhen submitted a memorial setting forth what was fitting in punishments and government.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen soon submitted a memorial on penal and administrative policy.

sentences.zh: 詔皆施行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that all be put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered all his proposals carried out.

sentences.zh: 熙平初，[4]加國珍使持節、都督、雍州刺史、驃騎大將軍、開府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiping, [4] Guozhen was further granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief, Governor of Yongzhou, Rapid Cavalry General, and establishment of a headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiping era, [4] Guozhen was further granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief, Governor of Yongzhou, Rapid Cavalry General, and the right to establish a headquarters.

sentences.zh: 靈太后以國珍年老，不欲令其在外，且欲示以方面之榮，竟不行。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling, because Guozhen was old, did not wish to have him go abroad, yet also wished to display to him the glory of a regional command; in the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling did not wish to send the aged Guozhen away from court, yet wanted to honor him with a regional command. In the end he never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒公，侍中如故，就宅拜之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Tutor, remaining Palace Attendant as before; the appointment was conferred at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Tutor while retaining his post as Palace Attendant. The appointment was conferred at his home.

sentences.zh: 靈太后、肅宗率百僚幸其第，宴會極歡。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling and Emperor Suzong led the hundred officials to visit his residence; the banquet reached the utmost joy.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling and Emperor Suzong led the court to his home for a lavish banquet.

sentences.zh: 又追京兆郡君為秦太上君。

translations.literal: Lady of Jingzhao Commandery was further posthumously honored as Grand Supreme Lady of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Lady of Jingzhao Commandery was further posthumously honored as Grand Supreme Lady of Qin.

sentences.zh: [5]太上君景明三年薨於洛陽，於此十六年矣。

translations.literal: [5] The Grand Supreme Lady had died in Luoyang in the third year of Jingming; it was now sixteen years since then.
translations.idiomatic: [5] The Grand Supreme Lady had died in Luoyang in the third year of Jingming—sixteen years had passed.

sentences.zh: 太后以太上君墳瘞卑局，更增廣，為起塋域門闕碑表。

translations.literal: The empress dowager, because the Grand Supreme Lady's tomb and burial were mean and cramped, further enlarged them and had a tomb precinct with gates, towers, steles, and markers raised.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager found the Grand Supreme Lady's tomb too modest and had the burial mound enlarged, with gates, towers, and steles erected.

sentences.zh: 侍中崔光等奏：「案漢高祖母始諡曰昭靈夫人，後為昭靈后，薄太后母曰靈文夫人，皆置園邑三百家，長丞奉守。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Cui Guang and others memorialized: "According to precedent, Emperor Gaozu of Han's mother was first given the posthumous title Lady Zhaoling, later Empress Zhaoling; Empress Dowager Bo's mother was titled Lady Lingwen—all had tomb estates of three hundred households, with chiefs and assistants to maintain them."
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Cui Guang and others memorialized: "By Han precedent, Emperor Gaozu's mother was first titled Lady Zhaoling, later Empress Zhaoling; Empress Dowager Bo's mother was titled Lady Lingwen. Each had a tomb estate of three hundred households with officials to maintain it."

sentences.zh: 今秦太上君未有尊諡，陵寢孤立，即秦君名，宜上終稱，兼設掃衞，以慰情典。

translations.literal: Now the Grand Supreme Lady of Qin has no honored posthumous title; her tomb stands alone. Following the name of the Lady of Qin, a final title should be granted, and tomb guardians established as well, to satisfy the demands of ritual feeling."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Supreme Lady of Qin has no posthumous title and her tomb lacks proper maintenance. She should receive a final honorific title and tomb guardians, in keeping with ritual propriety."

sentences.zh: 請上尊諡曰孝穆，權置園邑三十戶，立長丞奉守。

translations.literal: We request that the honored posthumous title Xiaomu be granted, and that a tomb estate of thirty households be provisionally established, with chiefs and assistants appointed to maintain it."
translations.idiomatic: We request the posthumous epithet Xiaomu and a provisional tomb estate of thirty households with officials to maintain it."

sentences.zh: 」太后從之。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager approved.

sentences.zh: 封國珍繼室梁氏為趙平郡君，元叉妻拜為女侍中，封新平郡君，又徙封馮翊君。

translations.literal: Guozhen's successor wife, the Lady Liang, was enfeoffed as Lady of Zhaoping Commandery; Yuan Cha's wife was appointed Lady Attendant and enfeoffed as Lady of Xinping Commandery, then transferred to Lady of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen's second wife, Lady Liang, was enfeoffed as Lady of Zhaoping Commandery. Yuan Cha's wife was appointed Lady Attendant and enfeoffed as Lady of Xinping Commandery, later transferred to Lady of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 國珍子祥妻長安縣公主，即清河王懌女也。

translations.literal: Guozhen's son Xiang's wife was the Princess of Chang'an County, who was the daughter of Prince of Qinghe, Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen's son Xiang married the Princess of Chang'an County, daughter of Prince of Qinghe Yi.

sentences.zh: 國珍年雖篤老，而雅敬佛法，時事齋潔，自強禮拜。

translations.literal: Although Guozhen was deeply aged, he elegantly revered the Buddhist Law, regularly observed fasting and purity, and by his own strength performed obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: Though deeply aged, Guozhen revered Buddhism, kept regular fasts, and still forced himself to perform prostrations.

sentences.zh: 至於出入侍從，猶能跨馬據鞍。

translations.literal: As for going out and in with attendants, he could still straddle a horse and grip the saddle.
translations.idiomatic: When he went abroad with his attendants, he could still mount a horse and ride.

sentences.zh: 神龜元年四月七日，步從所建佛像，發第至閶闔門四五里。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the fourth month of the first year of Shengui, he walked on foot following the Buddha image he had erected, from his residence to four or five li before the Changhe Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the fourth month of the first year of Shengui, he walked on foot behind the Buddha image he had commissioned, from his home to within four or five li of the Changhe Gate.

sentences.zh: 八日，又立觀像，晚乃肯坐。

translations.literal: On the eighth day he again stood viewing the image and only in the evening would consent to sit.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth he stood again to view the image and would not sit until evening.

sentences.zh: 勞熱增甚，因遂寢疾。

translations.literal: Fatigue and fever grew severe, and he thereupon took to his bed in illness.
translations.idiomatic: Exhaustion and fever worsened, and he took to his bed.

sentences.zh: 靈太后親侍藥膳。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling personally attended his medicines and food.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling personally tended his medicines and meals.

sentences.zh: 十二日薨，年八十。

translations.literal: On the twelfth he died, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the twelfth, aged eighty.

sentences.zh: 給東園溫明祕器、五時朝服各一具、衣一襲，贈布五千匹、錢一百萬、蠟千斤。

translations.literal: He was granted the secret funerary vessels of the Eastern Garden and Warm Brightness, one set each of court robes for the five seasons, and one suit of garments; there were granted five thousand bolts of cloth, a million cash, and a thousand jin of wax.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted imperial funerary vessels, one set of court robes for each season, and a full suit of garments, along with five thousand bolts of cloth, a million cash, and a thousand jin of wax.

sentences.zh: 大鴻臚持節監護喪事。

translations.literal: The Grand Herald, bearing the staff of authority, supervised the funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Herald supervised the funeral with imperial authority.

sentences.zh: 太后還宮，成服於九龍殿，遂居九龍寢室。

translations.literal: The empress dowager returned to the palace, completed mourning garments in the Hall of Nine Dragons, and then dwelt in the Nine Dragons sleeping chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager returned to the palace, donned mourning dress in the Hall of Nine Dragons, and took up residence in the Nine Dragons chamber.

sentences.zh: 肅宗服小功服，舉哀於太極東堂。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong wore the lesser mourning of five months and raised lamentation in the Eastern Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong wore five-month mourning and mourned in the Eastern Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 又詔自始薨至七七，皆為設千僧齋，令七人出家；

translations.literal: An edict also ordered that from the beginning of death until the forty-ninth day, a thousand-monk feast should be held on each occasion and seven persons be made to leave home;
translations.idiomatic: An edict also ordered that from the day of death until the forty-ninth day, a feast for a thousand monks should be held on each occasion and seven persons ordained;

sentences.zh: 百日設萬人齋，二七人出家。

translations.literal: on the hundredth day a ten-thousand-person feast was to be held, and twenty-seven persons were to leave home.
translations.idiomatic: on the hundredth day a feast for ten thousand was to be held, and twenty-seven persons ordained.

sentences.zh: 先是巫覡言將有凶，勸令為厭勝之法。

translations.literal: Earlier, shamans and diviners had said there would be misfortune and urged that methods of averting evil be performed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier shamans had foretold misfortune and urged protective rites.

sentences.zh: 國珍拒而不從，云吉凶有定分，唯修德以禳之。

translations.literal: Guozhen refused and would not follow, saying that fortune and misfortune have fixed allotments, and only by cultivating virtue can one avert them.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen refused, saying fortune and misfortune are ordained and can be averted only by cultivating virtue.

sentences.zh: 臨死與太后訣云：「母子善治天下，以萬人之心，勿視大臣面也。

translations.literal: At his death he took leave of the empress dowager, saying: "Mother and son, govern the realm well; with the heart of the myriad people—do not look to the faces of great ministers."
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he bade the empress dowager farewell: "Mother and son must govern the realm well. Rule with the hearts of the people in mind—do not defer to the faces of great ministers."

sentences.zh: 」殷勤至於再三。

translations.literal: " His earnestness reached to two and three times over.
translations.idiomatic: " He repeated this earnestly again and again.

sentences.zh: 又及其子祥，云：「我唯有一子，死後勿如比來威抑之。

translations.literal: He also spoke to his son Xiang, saying: "I have only one son; after my death do not, as of late, restrain him by severity."
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke to his son Xiang: "I have only one son. After my death, do not keep disciplining him as you have lately."

sentences.zh: 」靈太后以其好戲，時加威訓。

translations.literal: " Because Empress Dowager Ling, since he loved play, from time to time added stern admonition.
translations.idiomatic: " Empress Dowager Ling had often scolded Xiang for his love of play.

sentences.zh: 國珍故以為言。

translations.literal: Guozhen therefore spoke of this.
translations.idiomatic: That was why Guozhen spoke of it.

sentences.zh: 始國珍欲就祖父西葬舊鄉，後緣前世諸胡多在洛葬，有終洛之心。

translations.literal: At first Guozhen wished to follow his grandfather and be buried in the west in his native place; later, because former generations of various Hu had mostly been buried at Luoyang, he had the mind to end at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: At first Guozhen had wished to be buried in the west beside his grandfather in his native land. Later, seeing that many earlier Hu families had been buried at Luoyang, he came to favor burial there.

sentences.zh: 崔光嘗對太后前問國珍：「公萬年後為在此安厝，為歸長安？

translations.literal: Cui Guang once asked Guozhen before the empress dowager: "After your ten thousand years, will you be laid to rest here, or return to Chang'an?"
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang once asked Guozhen before the empress dowager: "After your ten thousand years, will you be laid to rest here, or return to Chang'an?"

sentences.zh: 」國珍言當陪葬天子山陵。

translations.literal: " Guozhen said he should be buried as a companion in the Son of Heaven's mountain tomb.
translations.idiomatic: " Guozhen said he wished to be buried beside the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 及病危，太后請以後事，竟言還安定，語遂昏忽。

translations.literal: When his illness was critical, the empress dowager asked about his last affairs; he finally said to return to Anding, and his words then became confused and dim.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell critically ill, the empress dowager asked his wishes. He finally said he wished to return to Anding, then lapsed into delirium.

sentences.zh: 太后問清河王懌與崔光等，議去留。

translations.literal: The empress dowager asked Prince of Qinghe, Yi, and Cui Guang and others to deliberate on whether to go or stay.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager consulted Prince of Qinghe Yi, Cui Guang, and others on whether to bury him at Luoyang or Anding.

sentences.zh: 懌等皆以病亂，請從先言。

translations.literal: Yi and the others all held that the illness had confused him and requested to follow his earlier words.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and the others held that delirium had confused his last words and urged following his earlier statement.

sentences.zh: 太后猶記崔光昔與國珍言，遂營墓於洛陽。

translations.literal: The empress dowager still remembered what Cui Guang had once said with Guozhen, and so had a tomb prepared at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager recalled Cui Guang's earlier conversation with Guozhen and had a tomb prepared at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 太后雖外從眾議，而深追臨終之語，云：「我公之遠慕二親，亦吾之思父母也。」

translations.literal: Although outwardly the empress dowager followed the multitude's counsel, inwardly she deeply recalled his dying words, saying: "My lord's longing from afar for his two parents is also my longing for my father and mother."
translations.idiomatic: Though she outwardly followed the court's advice, she deeply mourned his dying wish, saying, "My lord's longing for his parents in the west is like my own longing for my parents."

sentences.zh: 追崇假黃鉞、使持節、侍中、相國、都督中外諸軍事、太師、領太尉公、司州牧，號太上秦公，加九錫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored with the provisional yellow battle-axe, Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Chancellor of State, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies Within and Without, Grand Preceptor, concurrent Duke of Grand Marshal, and Governor of Sizhou; titled Grand Supreme Duke of Qin; and granted the Nine Bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored with the yellow battle-axe, Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Chancellor of State, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies Within and Without, Grand Preceptor, concurrent Duke of Grand Marshal, and Governor of Sizhou, titled Grand Supreme Duke of Qin, and granted the Nine Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 葬以殊禮，給九旒鑾輅，虎賁、班劍百人，前後部羽葆鼓吹，轀輬車；

translations.literal: He was buried with extraordinary rites: granted a carriage with nine tassels and imperial equipage, a hundred Tiger Guards with swords of office, feathered banners and drums in front and rear sections, and a hearse;
translations.idiomatic: He was buried with extraordinary rites: an imperial carriage with nine tassels, a hundred Tiger Guards with swords of office, feathered banners and drums before and behind, and a hearse;

sentences.zh: 諡文宣公；

translations.literal: posthumous title Duke Wenxuan;
translations.idiomatic: with the posthumous epithet Duke Wenxuan;

sentences.zh: 賜物三千段、粟一千五百石。

translations.literal: granted three thousand lengths of goods and fifteen hundred shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: and gifts of three thousand lengths of goods and fifteen hundred shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 又詔贈國珍祖父兄、父兄，下逮從子，皆有封職。

translations.literal: An edict also posthumously granted Guozhen's grandfather's elder brother, father's elder brother, and down to younger cousins—all received enfeoffment and office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also posthumously granted titles and offices to Guozhen's grandfather's elder brother, father's elder brother, and younger cousins.

sentences.zh: 持節就安定監護喪事。

translations.literal: A bearer of the staff of authority went to Anding to supervise the funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy with imperial authority went to Anding to supervise the funeral.

sentences.zh: [6]靈太后迎太上君神柩還第，與國珍俱葬，贈襚一與國珍同。

translations.literal: [6] Empress Dowager Ling welcomed the Grand Supreme Lady's spirit coffin back to the residence and buried her together with Guozhen; funeral gifts were granted equal to Guozhen's.
translations.idiomatic: [6] Empress Dowager Ling brought the Grand Supreme Lady's coffin home and buried her with Guozhen, with funeral gifts equal to his.

sentences.zh: 及國珍神主入廟，詔太常權給以軒懸之樂、六佾之舞。

translations.literal: When Guozhen's spirit tablet entered the temple, an edict ordered the Minister of Ceremonies provisionally to grant the suspended bells and stone chimes music and the six-rows dance.
translations.idiomatic: When Guozhen's spirit tablet entered the ancestral temple, the Minister of Ceremonies was ordered to provide suspended bells and the six-rows dance.

sentences.zh: 初國珍無男，養兄真子僧洗為後，後納趙平君，生子祥。

translations.literal: At first Guozhen had no son; he adopted his elder brother Zhen's son Sengxi as heir. Later he took Lady Zhaoping in marriage and begot the son Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: At first Guozhen had no son and adopted his brother Zhen's son Sengxi as heir. Later he married Lady Zhaoping and fathered Xiang.

sentences.zh: 僧洗，字湛輝。

translations.literal: Sengxi, styled Zhanhui.
translations.idiomatic: Sengxi, courtesy name Zhanhui.

sentences.zh: 封爰德縣公，位中書監、侍中，改封濮陽郡公。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Aide County, held the posts of Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat and Palace Attendant, and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Puyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Aide County, served as Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat and Palace Attendant, and was later re-enfeoffed as Duke of Puyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 僧洗自永安後廢棄，不預朝政。

translations.literal: From Yong'an onward Sengxi was cast aside and did not take part in court government.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yong'an era onward Sengxi was sidelined and took no part in government.

sentences.zh: 天平四年薨，詔給東園祕器，贈太師、太尉公、錄尚書事、雍州刺史，諡曰孝。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Tianping; an edict granted the secret vessels of the Eastern Garden; he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, Duke of Grand Marshal, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Yongzhou, with the posthumous title Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Tianping. An edict granted imperial funerary vessels and posthumously granted him Grand Preceptor, Duke of Grand Marshal, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Yongzhou, with the posthumous epithet Xiao.

sentences.zh: 真長子寧，[7]字惠歸。

translations.literal: Zhen's eldest son was Ning, [7] styled Huigui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's eldest son Ning, [7] courtesy name Huigui.

sentences.zh: 襲國珍先爵，改為臨涇伯，後進為公。

translations.literal: He inherited Guozhen's former title, which was changed to Earl of Linjing, and later was advanced to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited Guozhen's former title, which was changed to Earl of Linjing and later raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 歷岐涇二州刺史。

translations.literal: He successively held the governorships of Qi and Jing provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as governor of Qi and Jing provinces.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰孝穆。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Xiaomu.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous epithet Xiaomu.

sentences.zh: 女為清河王亶妃，生孝靜皇帝。

translations.literal: His daughter was consort to Prince of Qinghe, Dan, and bore Emperor Xiaojing.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter was consort to Prince of Qinghe Dan and bore Emperor Xiaojing.

sentences.zh: 武定初，贈太師、太尉公、錄尚書事，諡曰孝昭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuding, he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, Duke of Grand Marshal, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, with the posthumous title Xiaozhao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wuding era he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, Duke of Grand Marshal, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, with the posthumous epithet Xiaozhao.

sentences.zh: 子虔，字僧敬。

translations.literal: His son Qian, styled Sengjing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qian, courtesy name Sengjing.

sentences.zh: 元叉之廢靈太后，虔時為千牛備身，與備身張車渠等謀殺叉。

translations.literal: When Yuan Cha deposed Empress Dowager Ling, Qian was at the time a guard of the Thousand Oxen and, together with the guard Zhang Chequ and others, plotted to kill Cha.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Cha deposed Empress Dowager Ling, Qian was a guard of the Thousand Oxen and plotted with fellow guard Zhang Chequ and others to kill Cha.

sentences.zh: 事發，叉殺車渠等，虔坐遠徙。

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed, Cha killed Chequ and the others; Qian was punished by exile to a distant place.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, Cha killed Chequ and the others. Qian was exiled to a distant post.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，徵為吏部郎中。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power, he was summoned as Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power, he was recalled as Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 太后好以家人禮與親族宴戲，虔常致諫，由是後宴謔多不預焉。

translations.literal: The empress dowager liked to feast and jest with kin in the manner of a family household; Qian often offered remonstrance, and because of this afterward he was often not included in such banquets and sport.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager liked to feast and jest with kin in family fashion. Qian often remonstrated with her, and afterward was often excluded from such gatherings.

sentences.zh: 出為涇州刺史，封安陽縣侯。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Jingzhou and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to Jingzhou as governor and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anyang County.

sentences.zh: 興和三年，以帝元舅超遷司空公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xinghe, as the emperor's senior maternal uncle he was promoted over rank to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xinghe, as the emperor's senior maternal uncle he was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈太傅、太尉公、尚書僕射、徐州刺史，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Grand Tutor, Duke of Grand Marshal, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Xuzhou, with the posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted Grand Tutor, Duke of Grand Marshal, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Xuzhou, with the posthumous epithet Xuan.

sentences.zh: 葬日，百官會葬，乘輿送於郭外。

translations.literal: On the day of burial, the hundred officials attended the funeral; the imperial carriage escorted him beyond the outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of burial the hundred officials attended the funeral, and the imperial carriage escorted the coffin beyond the city wall.

sentences.zh: 子長粲。

translations.literal: His son was Changcan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Changcan.

sentences.zh: 李延寔，字禧，隴西人，尚書僕射沖之長子。

translations.literal: Li Yanshi, styled Xi, was a native of Longxi and the eldest son of Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanshi, courtesy name Xi, was a native of Longxi and the eldest son of Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Li Chong.

sentences.zh: 性溫良，少為太子舍人。

translations.literal: His nature was mild and good; in youth he was an Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was mild and good by nature and in youth served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，襲父爵清泉縣侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, he inherited his father's title as Marquis of Qingquan County.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shizong's reign he inherited his father's title as Marquis of Qingquan County.

sentences.zh: [8]累遷左將軍、光州刺史。

translations.literal: [8] He was repeatedly promoted to Left General and Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: [8] He rose in turn to Left General and Governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 莊帝即位，以元舅之尊，超授侍中、太保，封濮陽郡王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang ascended the throne, because of his rank as senior maternal uncle he was promoted over rank to Palace Attendant and Grand Guardian and enfeoffed as Prince of Puyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang came to the throne, Yanshi was promoted over rank to Palace Attendant and Grand Guardian as the emperor's senior maternal uncle, and enfeoffed as Prince of Puyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 延寔以太保犯祖諱，又以王爵非庶姓所宜，抗表固辭。

translations.literal: Yanshi, because Grand Guardian violated an ancestral taboo and because a princely title was not fitting for a common surname, submitted a memorial firmly declining.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi submitted a firm memorial of refusal, arguing that Grand Guardian violated an ancestral taboo and that a princely title was unsuitable for a commoner family.

sentences.zh: 徙封濮陽郡公，改授太傅。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Duke of Puyang Commandery and reappointed Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Puyang Commandery and appointed Grand Tutor instead.

sentences.zh: 尋轉司徒公，出為使持節、侍中、太傅、錄尚書事、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of Works and went out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Grand Tutor, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Minister of Works, then sent out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Grand Tutor, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尒朱兆入洛，乘輿幽縶，以延寔外戚，見害於州館。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang and the imperial carriage was held in secret confinement, because Yanshi was maternal kin he was killed in the provincial residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang and the emperor was held captive, Yanshi was killed at the provincial residence because he was imperial kin by marriage.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，歸葬洛陽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Chu's reign, his remains were returned for burial at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Chu's reign his remains were brought back for burial at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、侍中、太師、太尉公、錄尚書事、都督、雍州刺史，諡曰孝懿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, Duke of Grand Marshal, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Commander-in-Chief, and Governor of Yongzhou, with the posthumous title Xiaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, Duke of Grand Marshal, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Commander-in-Chief, and Governor of Yongzhou, with the posthumous epithet Xiaoyi.

sentences.zh: 長子彧，字子文，尚莊帝姊豐亭公主。

translations.literal: His eldest son was Yu, styled Ziwen, who married the Princess of Fengting, Emperor Zhuang's elder sister.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yu, courtesy name Ziwen, married the Princess of Fengting, Emperor Zhuang's elder sister.

sentences.zh: 封東平郡公，位侍中、左光祿大夫、中書監、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Dongping Commandery and held the posts of Palace Attendant, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, Rapid Cavalry General, and establishment of a headquarters with the Three Insignia, and Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Dongping Commandery and held the posts of Palace Attendant, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, Rapid Cavalry General, Honored with the Three Insignia and establishment of a headquarters, and Governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 彧任俠交遊，輕薄無行。

translations.literal: Yu was chivalrous and fond of making friends, frivolous and without proper conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was a chivalric rover who made many friends but was frivolous and dissolute.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮之死也，武毅之士皆彧所進。

translations.literal: At the death of Erzhu Rong, the martial and resolute men had all been introduced by Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong died, the bold warriors who struck him down had all been introduced by Yu.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，以罪棄市。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing's reign, he was executed by public display in the marketplace for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiaojing era he was executed in the marketplace for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：三五哲王，深防遠慮。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The sage kings of the Three Dynasties and the Five Emperors took deep precautions and looked far ahead.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: The sage kings of antiquity took deep precautions and looked far ahead.

sentences.zh: 舅甥之國，罕執鈞衡；

translations.literal: In states of uncles and nephews, few held the balance of power;
translations.idiomatic: In states ruled by uncles and nephews, few held the balance of power;

sentences.zh: 母后之家，無聞傾敗。

translations.literal: among families of empresses and empresses dowager, none were heard to topple and fail.
translations.idiomatic: and among families of empresses and empresses dowager, none were known to fall in ruin.

sentences.zh: 爰及後世，顛覆繼軌。

translations.literal: Reaching later ages, overthrow followed in the same track.
translations.idiomatic: In later ages, overthrow followed one after another.

sentences.zh: 蓋由進不以禮，故其斃亦速。

translations.literal: This was because advancement did not follow ritual; therefore their destruction was also swift.
translations.idiomatic: This was because they rose without proper ritual, and so their fall came swiftly.

sentences.zh: 其間或不泯舊基，[9]弗虧先構者，蓋處之以道，遠權之所致也。

translations.literal: Among them, some did not extinguish the old foundation, [9] nor impair what their forebears had built—this was because they were treated with the Way and because distant power was exercised.
translations.idiomatic: Among them, some did not destroy the old foundation [9] or impair what their forebears had built—because they were governed by principle and power was kept at a distance.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 魏書卷八十三下 諸本目錄此卷注「闕」字，卷末有宋人校語

translations.literal: Book of Wei, juan 83b: In the tables of contents of various editions this juan is marked with the character "deficient"; at the end of the juan there are collation notes by a Song person.
translations.idiomatic: Book of Wei, juan 83b: Various editions mark this juan as "deficient" in their tables of contents; Song-era collation notes appear at the end of the juan.

sentences.zh: 〈殿本入考證〉

translations.literal: 〈Entered into textual investigation in the Palace Edition〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Palace Edition, entered into textual investigation〉

sentences.zh: 云：「魏收書外戚傳亡，史臣論全用隋書外戚傳

translations.literal: It states: "Wei Shou's Book of Wei chapter on families of imperial consorts is lost; the historiographer's discussion wholly uses the chapter on families of imperial consorts in the Book of Sui
translations.idiomatic: It states: "Wei Shou's chapter on families of imperial consorts is lost; the historiographer's discussion is taken entirely from the Book of Sui chapter on families of imperial consorts

sentences.zh: 〈卷七九〉

translations.literal: 〈juan 79〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈juan 79〉

sentences.zh: 」按此卷亦以北史卷八０外戚傳補。

translations.literal: " According to this, the present juan was also supplemented from the chapter on families of imperial consorts in Beishi juan 80.
translations.idiomatic: " This juan was also supplemented from the chapter on families of imperial consorts in the History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 80.

sentences.zh: 其于勁傳採北史卷三一于栗磾附于勁傳，李延寔傳採卷一００自序。

translations.literal: Its biography of Yu Jin draws on the appended biography of Yu Jin in Beishi juan 31 under Yu Lidi; the biography of Li Yanshi draws on the autobiographical preface in juan 100.
translations.idiomatic: The biography of Yu Jin draws on the appended biography in the History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 31, under Yu Lidi; the biography of Li Yanshi draws on the autobiographical preface in juan 100.

sentences.zh: 諸傳均有溢出語，當是以高氏小史等他書附益之。

translations.literal: All the biographies contain superfluous passages, which must have been added from other books such as the Brief History of the Gao Clan.
translations.idiomatic: All the biographies contain passages not found in the main sources, probably added from works such as the Brief History of the Gao Clan.

sentences.zh: 自栗磾至勁

translations.literal: From Li Dili to Jin
translations.idiomatic: From Li Dili to Jin

translations.literal: 〈to〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈to〉

sentences.zh: 三開國公 按此數語魏書本在卷三一于栗磾附于忠傳後，北史卷二三于栗磾傳移在于勁傳中，則在後的于忠所歷官爵，不當計算在內，所舉贈公、領軍、尚書令、開國公便都少了一人，實誤。

translations.literal: three founding marquises. According to this, these words originally stood in the Book of Wei after the appended biography of Yu Zhong under Yu Lidi in juan 31; the Beishi biography of Yu Lidi in juan 23 moved them into the biography of Yu Jin. Then the offices and titles held by the later Yu Zhong should not be counted within; the cited posthumous dukes, commanders of the guards, directors of the masters of writing, and founding marquises are each one person short—an actual error.
translations.idiomatic: three founding marquises. In the Book of Wei these words originally followed the appended biography of Yu Zhong under Yu Lidi in juan 31; the History of the Northern Dynasties moved them into the biography of Yu Jin. Yu Zhong's later offices should not be counted here, so each category—posthumous dukes, commanders of the guards, directors of the masters of writing, and founding marquises—is one short. This is an error.

sentences.zh: 此傳以北史補，不記卷三一已有此語，以致複出。

translations.literal: This biography was supplemented from the Beishi without noting that juan 31 already contained this language, causing duplication.
translations.idiomatic: Because this biography was supplemented from the History of the Northern Dynasties without noting that juan 31 already contained this passage, it appears twice.

sentences.zh: 參卷三一校記[九]。

translations.literal: See collation note [9] to juan 31.
translations.idiomatic: See collation note [9] to juan 31.

sentences.zh: 高平郡都將 按郡無都將，「郡」當是「鎮」之訛。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief of Gaoping Commandery. According to this, commanderies had no commanders-in-chief; "commandery" should be a corruption of "garrison."
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-Chief of Gaoping Commandery. Commanderies had no such office; "commandery" is likely a corruption of "garrison."

sentences.zh: 熙平初 諸本及北史卷八０胡國珍傳「熙平」作「延和」，通志卷一六五胡國珍傳作「熙平中」。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiping. In various editions and in the Beishi biography of Hu Guozhen in juan 80, "Xiping" is written as "Yanhe"; in the Comprehensive Gazetteer, juan 165, biography of Hu Guozhen, it reads "in Xiping."
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiping. Various editions and the History of the Northern Dynasties biography of Hu Guozhen, juan 80, read "Yanhe" instead of "Xiping"; the Comprehensive Gazetteer, juan 165, reads "during Xiping."

sentences.zh: 按事見卷九肅宗紀熙平元年八月乙巳，延和乃拓跋燾年號，遠在其前。

translations.literal: According to this, the event appears in the annals of Emperor Suzong in juan 9, eighth month, day yisi of the first year of Xiping; Yanhe is the reign title of Tuoba Tao, far earlier.
translations.idiomatic: The event appears in the annals of Emperor Suzong, juan 9, on day yisi of the eighth month of the first year of Xiping. Yanhe is the reign title of Tuoba Tao, much earlier.

sentences.zh: 今據通志改作「熙平」。

translations.literal: Now, following the Comprehensive Gazetteer, it is changed to "Xiping."
translations.idiomatic: Following the Comprehensive Gazetteer, we emend to "Xiping."

sentences.zh: 事在元年，「初」字不誤。

translations.literal: The event was in the first year; the character "beginning" is not in error.
translations.idiomatic: The event occurred in the first year; "early" is correct.

sentences.zh: 又追京兆郡君為秦太上君 按「追」下當脫「贈」或「尊」「崇」字。

translations.literal: Further posthumously honoring Lady of Jingzhao Commandery as Grand Supreme Lady of Qin. According to this, after "posthumously" there should be a missing character such as "grant," "honor," or "exalt."
translations.idiomatic: Further posthumously honoring Lady of Jingzhao Commandery as Grand Supreme Lady of Qin. After "posthumously" a word such as "grant," "honor," or "exalt" is probably missing.

sentences.zh: 持節就安定監護喪事 按胡國珍死和葬都在洛陽，何故「就安定監護喪事」？

translations.literal: Bearing the staff of authority, going to Anding to supervise funeral affairs. According to this, Hu Guozhen died and was buried both at Luoyang—why "going to Anding to supervise funeral affairs"?
translations.idiomatic: Bearing the staff of authority, going to Anding to supervise funeral affairs. Hu Guozhen died and was buried at Luoyang—why "going to Anding to supervise funeral affairs"?

sentences.zh: 下文云：「迎太上君神柩還第」，疑「安定」下脫「公第」二字。

translations.literal: The text below says, "welcoming the Grand Supreme Lady's spirit coffin back to the residence"; it is suspected that after "Anding" the two characters "duke's residence" are missing.
translations.idiomatic: The text below says, "welcoming the Grand Supreme Lady's spirit coffin back to the residence." The two characters "duke's residence" are probably missing after "Anding."

sentences.zh: 真長子寧 諸本「真」字連上段「諡曰孝」，「長子寧」提行。

translations.literal: Zhen's eldest son Ning. In various editions the character "Zhen" is joined to the preceding passage "posthumous title Xiao," and "eldest son Ning" begins a new line.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's eldest son Ning. In various editions "Zhen" is joined to the preceding "posthumous epithet Xiao," and "eldest son Ning" begins a new line.

sentences.zh: 成為胡僧洗諡「孝真」，「寧」是僧洗的長子。

translations.literal: This made it appear that Hu Sengxi's posthumous title was "Xiaozhen," and that "Ning" was Sengxi's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: This made it appear that Hu Sengxi's posthumous epithet was Xiaozhen and that Ning was Sengxi's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 按真乃國珍兄，見上文，寧乃僧洗兄。

translations.literal: According to this, Zhen was Guozhen's elder brother, as seen above; Ning was Sengxi's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: In fact Zhen was Guozhen's elder brother, as stated above; Ning was Sengxi's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 北史原文本不提行，後人寫刻魏書則凡附見諸子孫無不提行，這裏由於誤讀，提行亦謬，致以兄為子，今改正。

translations.literal: The original Beishi text did not begin a new line; when later people copied and carved the Book of Wei, they invariably began new lines for all appended sons and grandsons. Here, because of misreading, the line break is also wrong, causing an elder brother to be taken as a son; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The original History of the Northern Dynasties text did not break the line here. Later copyists of the Book of Wei always began new lines for appended descendants; misreading here wrongly made an elder brother appear as a son. This is now corrected.

sentences.zh: 襲父爵清泉縣侯 按卷五三李沖傳，沖封「清淵縣侯」。

translations.literal: Inherited his father's title as Marquis of Qingquan County. According to the biography of Li Chong in juan 53, Chong was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qingyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: Inherited his father's title as Marquis of Qingquan County. The biography of Li Chong in juan 53 records his enfeoffment as Marquis of Qingyuan County.

sentences.zh: 「清淵」為漢以來舊縣，卷一０六上地形志上，屬司州陽平郡。

translations.literal: "Qingyuan" is an old county since Han; in the Treatise on Geography, part 1, juan 106, it belonged to Yangping Commandery in Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan was an old county name since Han; the Treatise on Geography, juan 106, places it in Yangping Commandery, Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 此傳以北史補，避唐諱改「泉」。

translations.literal: This biography was supplemented from the Beishi; to avoid Tang taboo, "yuan" was changed to "quan."
translations.idiomatic: This biography was supplemented from the History of the Northern Dynasties; "yuan" was changed to "quan" to avoid Tang taboo.

sentences.zh: 其間或不泯舊基 諸本「泯」上有「斃」字。

translations.literal: Among them, some did not extinguish the old foundation. In various editions, above "extinguish" there is the character "destroy."
translations.idiomatic: Among them, some did not extinguish the old foundation. Various editions have the character "destroy" before "extinguish."

sentences.zh: 此傳本出北史，北史傳論又本隋書卷七九外戚傳論，今檢隋書、北史都作「今或不隕舊基」，這裏「今或」作「其間」，「隕」作「泯」，均兩通，「斃」字則涉上「其斃亦速」而衍，今刪。

translations.literal: This chapter originally came from the Beishi; the Beishi discussion in turn derives from the discussion in the Book of Sui, juan 79, on families of imperial consorts. Checking now, both the Book of Sui and the Beishi read "now some do not fall from the old foundation"; here "now some" is written as "among them," and "fall" as "extinguish"—both are acceptable. The character "destroy" is a derivative from the preceding "their destruction is also swift"; it is now deleted.
translations.idiomatic: This chapter derives from the History of the Northern Dynasties, whose discussion in turn comes from the Book of Sui, juan 79. Both the Book of Sui and the History of the Northern Dynasties read "now some do not fall from the old foundation"; here "now some" appears as "among them" and "fall" as "extinguish"—both acceptable. The character "destroy" is a spurious addition from the preceding "their fall comes swiftly" and is deleted.
